chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Dawud al-Raqqi said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina when a man entered and said, 'Indeed, a group arrived today and their Hajj was missed.' He said, 'We ask Allah for well-being; I see that each one of them should shed the blood of a sheep, become free from ihram restrictions, and Hajj will be obligatory upon them next year if they return to their lands. And if they stay until the days of Tashreeq pass in Mecca, until they exit to the time of the people of Mecca, enter ihram from there, and perform Umrah, then Hajj will not be obligatory upon them next year.'

key_terms.اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the options for making up a missed Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the specific legal remedies for those who missed the Hajj season, offering a choice between expiation via animal sacrifice with a deferred makeup Hajj, or remaining in Mecca to perform Umrah to avoid the future obligation. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of ritual purification and the conditions under which the primary obligation of Hajj is considered fulfilled or deferred. The distinction between staying until the people of Mecca depart versus waiting for the days of Tashriq to conclude underscores the precise temporal boundaries for valid ritual status.
